notes:
Account snapshot: Springcliff is a product-led mid-market SaaS (customer comms platform) building a context-aware chat assistant + semantic search across product docs. They started on Hosted API to move fast, now evaluating Dedicated for predictable throughput and data separation.

Key asks from product team: low p95 chat latency, deterministic unit cost for budgeting, ability to pin model versions, and EU data residency for parts of the dataset. Security/Legal asks: SSO (SAML), SOC2 evidence, audit logging, KMS integration for key encryption, retention controls.

Cost optimization workshop (2026-01-15) notes:
- Attendees: Evan (AE), Priya (SE), Springcliff: CTO (R. Gomez), Lead ML Eng (N. Patel), Product PM (L. Huang)
- Agenda: baseline cost for Hosted POC, Dedicated sizing, batching/caching overview, quantization trade-offs, unit economics model for 12-month commit.
- Findings: dynamic batching + prefix KV cache can reduce per-token compute by ~30-45% on their chat workload; Q8 quantization on the 13B model shows ~35% throughput improvement with ~1-2% observed quality delta on our eval set; using a smaller reranker model for top-50 candidates saves 60% of reranking cost with negligible impact to precision@10.
- Action items from workshop: run Dedicated POC with batch size profile [8,16,32], enable KV cache for session prefixes, test Q8_0 quant profile vs fp16 on Redwood-verified 13B, capture unit economics per 1M tokens.

Quotes / call snippets: "If we can get predictable token costs and a drop-in path to dedicated, we can sign for a year" — Springcliff CTO. "Need the math to show 12-mo commit is cheaper than burst on Hosted for our scale" — Head of Ops.

POC scope (high level): functional parity check on Hosted -> Dedicated, performance sweep (latency/throughput) with service-level traffic replay, cost model export, and SSO + KMS integration test. POC success metrics: p95 chat latency <=150ms, cost per 1M tokens under $800 (target), can sustain 200 concurrent chat sessions with autoscaling.

Risks/concerns: procurement insists on SOC2 report; engineering concerned about tail latency during multi-tenant bursts; legal wants an explicit EU-residency clause for customer transcripts.
